report.body:
The operation began on the night of Wednesday 4 November after an anonymous tip
that a vehicle was being used to sell drugs in Água Clara. The tip
concerned a white VW Gol allegedly used to sell drugs in Jardim das Palmeiras. When Military Police located the car, its driver tried to flee but was
stopped after a chase over several blocks. Officers found suspected cocaine
in the car and cannabis portions, a precision scale, packaging materials and
cash at the driver's home. The joint follow-up found two other suspects at
a snack bar and 59 bricks of material resembling marijuana that weighed about 54
kg.

Investigators later found a third suspect with approximately 500 grams of
marijuana and a precision scale. Police also recovered a bag of 19 portions
of cocaine, about 120 grams in total, which investigators said the first suspect
had discarded during the original approach. A 28-year-old man under
investigation for trafficking and wanted on an outstanding arrest warrant was
also located and arrested. RCN67 reported five men arrested in total: four
were booked in flagrante for trafficking and association for trafficking, while
the fifth was arrested under a judicial order. Officers seized a car, a
motorcycle, three scales, three mobile phones, packaging material and about
R$250, in addition to the drugs.

Sohag Criminal Court sentenced three defendants to death by hanging for hashish
trafficking and a scalpel offense in Maragha district. The court ordered
the defendants to pay case expenses and confiscated the seized items. The
case dates to November 2025, when three people were accused of possessing
hashish for trafficking and carrying a scalpel without legal justification in
Maragha.

Ahl Masr reported that all three defendants came from El-Ghanayem in Asyut
Governorate. The case papers listed number 16693 of 2025 for Maragha and
number 3346 of 2025 for North Sohag. Ahl Masr said anti-narcotics officers
from Central Upper Egypt's Sohag branch arrested the three after prosecutors
authorized a search of the first defendant. A chemical-laboratory report
identified the seized material as hashish and counted 280 pieces in three lots
of 80, 150 and 50, plus a plastic sack with traces. A prosecution
inspection linked the car where drugs were found to the first defendant's
physical control; prosecutors also accused him of possessing a scalpel without
legal justification.

The Public Prosecution referred the case to Sohag Criminal Court after
completing its investigation. The court referred the defendants' papers to
Egypt's Grand Mufti for a religious opinion on hanging. After the Mufti's
opinion, the court imposed the three death sentences unanimously.

report.body:
Mossos d’Esquadra officers arrested seven men aged 29 to 55 at an industrial
warehouse in Cabanes on 1 October 2026 and seized 8,025 kilograms of hashish. Surveillance had shown people and vehicles visiting the warehouse
occasionally, even though there was no apparent business or work activity there. In early October, officers saw repeated movements of people and vans, an
articulated truck arrive, and people changing vehicle plates to make
identification harder.

When officers entered the warehouse, they found seven people unloading pallets
from the truck and intending to move the hashish into vans for later
distribution. The hashish was hidden among cargo inside large raffia sacks
loaded with rubber crumb, a method used to make it harder to detect at police or
customs checks. Investigators described the warehouse as a logistics base
used solely for drug trafficking. Officers also found a firearm in one of
the detainees’ vans.

Police valued the hashish at more than €16.2 million on the illicit market.
The seven detainees were brought before the Figueres Civil and Investigative
Section of the Court of First Instance. Four were remanded in provisional
detention without bail and the other three in provisional detention with bail. The investigation remained open, with Mossos not ruling out further arrests
or related operations.

report.title: Ceuta truck driver remanded after hashish seizure at port
report.summary: Spain's UDYCO arrested a truck driver at the port of Ceuta after finding hashish hidden in a false compartment in his truck; the official weight was not disclosed and unofficial estimates differ. A judicial authority ordered the driver's pretrial detention on 15 November for an offence against public health.
report.body:
Spain's UDYCO drug unit arrested a truck driver at the port of Ceuta carrying a
stash of hashish hidden in a sophisticated false bottom. Officers
intercepted the truck on the port road at the Muelle de Poniente and searched it
with support from the UPR prevention unit and the canine group. They found
the hashish and detained the driver, showing him the drugs found in the vehicle
he was driving.

The truck appeared empty and was heading toward boarding for Spain when a
specialist drugs dog alerted, prompting an exhaustive hours-long search inside
and outside the vehicle. After the hours-long detailed inspection, officers
found a large number of bags full of hashish inside the truck's structure.
Officers recovered numerous bags of hashish from the trailer's false bottom,
with first estimates putting the haul above 300 kilograms although police gave
no official weight. The submitted account describes the seizure as about
300 kilograms of hashish arriving from Morocco.

The handcuffed driver was taken to police headquarters and placed under
investigation for an offence against public health. Police link the
operation to open UDYCO investigations into groups moving hashish from Ceuta to
mainland Spain in heavy vehicles with hidden compartments. A judicial authority ordered the driver's pretrial detention for an offence against public health on Sunday, 15 November.

total, or about 3.24 hectares. The farms contained approximately 53,000
suspected cannabis plants, ranging from two to six feet tall.

areas contained 10 pounds (about 4.54 kg) of dried cannabis ready for the
market. Police destroyed the plants, dried cannabis, camps and drying areas
by fire. Police estimated the total value of the narcotics destroyed at GYD
$22,038,728. No arrests were made during the exercise. The Guyana
Police Force said investigations into the operation were continuing.

report.body:
Three Thai nationals were arrested at Bandaranaike International Airport (BIA)
in Katunayake for allegedly trying to smuggle hashish into Sri Lanka.
Police Narcotics Bureau officers made the arrests early on 15 October, while the
suspects were attempting to leave the airport with the narcotics. The three
suspects, aged 22, 22 and 33, were reportedly employed as drivers in Thailand. They had arrived at Katunayake Airport from Bangkok at approximately 12.30
a.m. aboard Thai Airways flight TG-307. A search of their luggage uncovered
5 kilograms and 96 grams (5.096 kilograms) of hashish in three travel bags.

The hashish was concealed inside containers of cosmetic products, including
cosmetic cream containers. The seizure was valued at approximately Rs. 51
million. The three suspects, together with the seized hashish, were
scheduled to be produced before the Negombo Magistrate’s Court on 15 October for
further investigations. The Police Narcotics Bureau at Katunayake Airport
said its officers were conducting further investigations into the case.

report.body:
Police in Ajdabiya arrested two suspects and referred both to the public
prosecutor after raiding a residential apartment in the city. Ajdabiya
Security's photo caption dates the raid to 22 October 2026. The searched
apartment was on the third floor of a residential building in the city.

The Criminal Investigation Department of the Ajdabiya Security Directorate acted
on information from private sources that narcotics and hallucinogenic pills were
in the apartment. The tip said the items were to be moved to an unknown
place to hide them and cover up distribution activity. Investigators opened
an inquiry, checked the information, notified the department and
investigation-unit chiefs, informed the public prosecutor and obtained legal
authorization before searching the apartment. The search yielded 2
kilograms of hashish, 59 boxes of tramadol containing 5,529 tablets and LYD
16,500 in cash. Another account gave the tramadol total as 39 boxes
containing 3,690 tablets.

The seized goods were hidden in a bag designed to carry children, and the
suspects were taken to the department's headquarters to complete
evidence-gathering procedures. The police unit said the suspects admitted
what was attributed to them during evidence-gathering before referral to the
Public Prosecution for legal action.

report.body:
On 19 October 2026, immigration police searched a rented three-storey house in
Soi Khu Bon 27, Yaek 14, Tha Raeng, Bang Khen, Bangkok, under a Min Buri
Criminal Court warrant. Officers arrested one Vietnamese man and four
Myanmar nationals who were sorting cannabis buds for packaging and distribution
to customers. Police found numerous black bags of cannabis buds across all
three floors, with the seizure weighing more than five tonnes. The house
had a ventilation system designed to expel the cannabis odor outside.

Residents' complaints about a strong cannabis smell prompted the investigation. Thairath reported that officers spent about two months gathering evidence
before the raid. Bangkok Post described the investigation as year-long. The Myanmar workers were reportedly paid 200 to 300 baht a day for sorting
and packing the buds. The operators held a cannabis-processing licence
valid only for Nong Bua Lamphu province, not Bangkok.

The house was used to store, sort and package cannabis buds before distribution
to customers. Officials said the seized buds would be sent for laboratory
testing to determine whether they were grown locally or imported. Police
were seeking the Thai person who signed the lease and tracing the other people
involved in the operation.

report.body:
Unit No. 2 of the Mykolaiv District Police Department uncovered the 51-year-old
man's activity in July 2026 and carried out an authorised search of his home. The search found and seized more than 10 kilograms of dried narcotic
material and 14 cannabis plants. Police said he grew cannabis on his home
plot, fertilising the soil, clearing weeds and watering the plants regularly. He dried part of the crop in the house attic and ground and packed another
part in glass jars for storage and, investigators said, sale.

Police detained him under Ukraine's criminal procedure code and notified him of
suspicion of storing narcotics for sale in an especially large amount and
cultivating cannabis. Investigators sent all the seized narcotic material
for expert examination.

Police said the court found him guilty of the offences. The court sentenced
him to nine years in prison. The police said the judgment had not yet
entered into force.

Saratoga County sheriff’s deputies arrested Kevin C. Wilbur, 46, of Brushton,
and Quinton L. Carle, 23, of Bombay after a traffic stop on the Northway in
Clifton Park. The vehicle was stopped at about 2:30 p.m. on Tuesday,
September 8, 2026, for following another car too closely and having insufficient
tail lights. The sheriff’s office said deputies seized 489 pounds (about
221.81 kilograms) of cannabis after the stop.

Wilbur was also cited for following too closely and having insufficient tail
lamps. Both men were arraigned before Judge Jennifer Jeram in Clifton Park
Town Court. Wilbur was remanded to Saratoga County Jail while Carle was
released on his own recognizance pending further proceedings. Sheriff
Jeffrey R. Brown said deputies had prevented nearly one-quarter ton of illicit
cannabis from reaching the streets.
